questions.scenario: Which statement covers a PERIOD of time, and which freezes an INSTANT?
options: Income Statement & Cash Flow cover a period; Balance Sheet freezes one moment
Only Balance Sheet covers a period
questions.explanation: 'For the year ended...' vs 'AS AT 31 December' — the wording on every real statement reflects this. Mixing up the shapes causes endless misreading.
wrongExplanations: Balance sheet is a photograph, not a film.
P&L and CF are films (flows); BS is the photo (stock).
Time-shape is fundamental to reading any financial report.

questions.scenario: How does the year's net profit reach the Balance Sheet?
options: Via retained earnings inside EQUITY: profit adds to owners' stake after dividends
questions.explanation: This IS the binding secret: P&L result rolls into equity, keeping Assets = Liabilities + Equity intact. Every balanced entry since Module 1 was quietly guaranteeing this link.
wrongExplanations: The three cameras film ONE story — their linkage is their power.
Profit ≠ cash (Module 9's whole mystery).
Depreciation is an expense flow, not the profit-transfer channel.

questions.scenario: Cash flow statement ADDS BACK depreciation because:
options: It reduced profit but consumed NO cash — adding it back shows true operating cash generation before investing outflows
questions.explanation: Module 10's non-cash expense resolved: profit included it; cash didn't feel it; CF reconciles by adding back, then separately shows machine PURCHASES under investing.
wrongExplanations: It's mandatory matching arithmetic, never optional.
The add-back is reconciliation, not decoration.
Machine purchases appear as INVESTING outflows — nothing refunds anything.

questions.scenario: 12Cr profit but only 40L new cash. The biggest culprit per the worked example:
options: Working capital growth — receivables and inventory absorbed crores as the business grew
questions.explanation: Growth parks profit into promises and products: receivables +9.8Cr, inventory +6.2Cr against the year's earnings. Fast-growing factories die of this exact arithmetic — hence forecast discipline.
wrongExplanations: Salaries were already fully expensed within the 12Cr figure.
Tax lines matter but were small next to working-capital absorption here.
Fees are rounding errors at this scale.

questions.scenario: A bank asks 'how much do you owe suppliers TODAY?' Which source answers authoritatively?
options: AP control account + supplier subledger detail AS OF today (balance-sheet family)
questions.explanation: Owed-today is an instant question → Balance Sheet layer, with subledger detail underneath (Module 3). Statements are COMPUTED from live ledgers, never stored separately.
wrongExplanations: Period statements say nothing about this morning.
Production reports count shirts, not debts.
Forecasts project FUTURE cash; they don't state current liabilities.

questions.scenario: INV-8891 ships Aug 15. By year-end, which statements have felt it?
options: All three: P&L (revenue+COGS), Balance Sheet (receivable/inventory shift, then retained profit), Cash Flow (collection in operating)
questions.explanation: One shipment ripples through everything: earned in August's P&L, carried as receivable on interim balance sheets, collected through operating cash flow, finally settled into retained earnings. One story, three cameras.
wrongExplanations: Recognition happened at B/L date regardless of collection timing — waiting for cash is Module 9 thinking, not recognition.
The P&L felt it first (August revenue and COGS); the balance sheet carried the receivable and inventory shift all along.
Internal reports mirror the statutory three: if only internal reports showed it, the audited statements would be wrong.

questions.scenario: Why must ERP statements be COMPUTED from GL rather than typed/edited reports?
options: Because statements inherit honesty from entries: computed figures stay consistent with subledgers and reconcile across all three — edited reports can drift from truth silently
questions.explanation: Statement = query over classified balances (that's WHY COA types exist). Manual statement editing recreates the March/April lie at the highest level — and auditors test exactly this consistency.
wrongExplanations: Speed is trivial beside integrity.
Aesthetics are templates, not generation method.
Beauty without lineage is how fraud dresses.

questions.scenario: Gross margin fell from 19% to 15% quarter-on-quarter. Best FIRST investigation:
options: Drill COGS composition per buyer/style — mix shift? costing errors? unabsorbed overhead? yarn price spike? — using order-level costing data from Module 5
Adjust last quarter's numbers to compare better
questions.explanation: Margins move for traceable reasons; order-level cost rollups reveal which. Restating history to flatter comparison is falsification, not analysis.
wrongExplanations: Punishment before diagnosis guarantees ignorance continues.
Software computes what data says — first ask what the DATA says.
Rewriting history destroys trend integrity forever.

questions.scenario: Which single check BEST proves the three statements agree?
options: Closing cash on the cash flow statement equals bank balance on the balance sheet AND net profit ties into equity movement
questions.explanation: Those cross-ties ARE the agreement: CF ends where BS cash stands; P&L result sits inside equity. Auditors test these joints precisely because mismatches expose upstream breaks.
wrongExplanations: Branding proves branding.
Cosmetics again — content linkage is the proof.
Signatures attest review, not mathematical coherence.

questions.scenario: The MD wants 'one number' summarizing company health. Most professional response:
options: Give profit only — everyone understands it
Refuse the oversimplification: present all three statements with the two binding checks explained — health is a STORY with three required camera angles
Give cash only — survival matters most
questions.explanation: Single-number health summaries caused countless factory failures ('profitable' while starving). Leadership deserves — and can learn — the full three-camera story you can now tell.
wrongExplanations: Profit alone hides cash starvation (this module's opening mystery!).
Cash alone hides erosion of margins and asset base over time.
Arithmetic soup serves no decision-maker.
